winner.text: Replace row-averaged BCE with user-normalized BCE so each user's training impressions contribute equal total loss mass.
winner.rationale: The official objective is within-user, while the current trainer averages loss over shuffled rows. Official validation has 22,377 users and shows materially heterogeneous slice quality, so reducing domination by prolific users is a direct alignment test without introducing a new feature family.
winner.exact_ablation: Change only the BCE reduction: weight each training row by the inverse number of training impressions for its user, normalized to mean weight one; keep features, additive scorer, optimizer, batch size, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.004 from closer within-user objective alignment.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.001 to +0.002; equal-user weighting may reduce emphasis on high-volume users that supply many top-five examples.

selection_rationale: Select c01. It is the consultant's top-ranked candidate (utility 8.2) and offers the most reliable scarce-experiment tradeoff: a tightly isolated, low-runtime, low-leakage correction to the mismatch between row-mean BCE training and the official within-user evaluation. The parent validation covers 22,377 users and shows heterogeneous user-frequency slices, so preventing prolific users from dominating loss mass is directly supported and broadly applicable. Although its expected primary gain (+0.0015) is lower than some higher-variance ranking and interaction alternatives, its stronger confidence, minimal downside, and unchanged features/scorer make it the preferred dependable improvement.
